claim: The supplier specifies Invitrogen F8801 microspheres as 0.1 um in diameter (nominal).

identifiers.product: FluoSpheres Carboxylate-Modified Microspheres, 0.1 um, red fluorescent (580/605)
identifiers.applies_to: the type F8801. Applying it to the beads on this bench goes through the E5 linking claim particle_suspension_b_identity, which a card applying this to the bench must cite alongside it and which fixes the grade at E5 by 5.8

validity_conditions: A NOMINAL SIZE CLASS, NOT A MEASURED MEAN. The page prints `0.1 um` for the product and says a Certificate of Analysis exists per lot; the certificate is where a measured mean diameter and its spread would come from, and without the lot number nobody can say which certificate applies. So this is one significant figure and order_of_magnitude precision: it places the beads in the 100 nm decade and claims nothing finer. No spread is printed and none is asserted. Named tracer_diameter because that is the quantity the cards asked for; the 5 um bottle's tracer_diameter_measured answers to the same name, and the subject and catalogue number are what tell the two apart -- a caller must read them, not take the first hit. THIS IS ABOUT THE TYPE, NOT THE BOTTLE. Under the instance/type split, F8801 is a type and its facts are ordinary entries at E3 from the supplier; the beads on the bench are the instance particle_suspension_b, and the claim joining them is particle_suspension_b_identity at E5, because the person named the product by pasting this page and did not read the bottle. Anything here applied to the bench inherits E5. READ BY THIS SEAT, NOT ONLY PASTED. The person's paste (microscope_agent/questions/mic-20260930-001/asked_of_the_person.jsonl at 51c61eb) is what identified the product; the values here were read by this seat off the vendor's own page on 2026-10-01 and agree with the paste on every field, which is why this is spec: at E3 and not a copy of a copy.

numbers.name: tracer_diameter
numbers.note: the supplier's nominal size for the product, one significant figure. A lot certificate would give a measured mean.
